sources.entry: Apprise API | Send notifications to 100+ services through a single API

summary.one_liner: Apprise API is a self-hosted REST gateway that lets you send notifications to 150+ services through HTTP calls, with a built-in configuration web UI.
summary.what_it_does: Wraps the Apprise notification library in a Docker-deployable HTTP service. A stateless /notify endpoint sends messages (with optional attachments) to URLs supplied in the request or in an environment variable. A stateful mode lets you save Apprise configurations under a Config ID key and send through them by key, with tags to target groups of services. A small web Configuration Manager lets you create, test and review saved configurations. Optional features described in the README include Basic Auth with access modes, Prometheus metrics at /metrics, a /status health check, live progress streaming via server-sent events, and template values in saved YAML configs. The README also mentions an Android companion app (Apprise Mobile) that connects to your server.
use_cases: Send alerts from scripts or infrastructure to many services at once
Run a self-hosted notification gateway on a home or internal network
Store notification endpoints centrally and reference them by key
Route notifications to groups of services using tags
Send messages with file attachments through a simple HTTP call
Test and verify Apprise URL configurations in a browser
how_to_run: Open the web interface on port 8000 in a browser to manage configurations
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d (example compose file in README)
notable: Single HTTP API in front of 150+ notification services via Apprise URLs
Stateless mode needs no storage; stateful mode persists configs under a key
Tag expressions (AND with spaces, OR with commas) to target subsets of destinations
Container-native logging to stdout and a hardened read-only runtime example
Prometheus /metrics endpoint and JSON /status health check
caveats: Authentication is disabled by default and must be enabled with APPRISE_AUTH_REQUIRED=yes
Official container images are published for amd64, arm/v7 and arm64 only
Mobile app requires a running Apprise API server; it is not standalone
